page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and is supported by a cache hierarchy including 32 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 786 GB volume, and the system is Premium Storage capable, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and image processing also demonstrate high-tier execution speeds. Memory performance is robust, with Passmark memory scores in the top tier, although uncached memory read and write bandwidth tests fall within the average range. Cryptographic operations perform exceptionally well due to hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions. However, while small-model LLM text generation is highly efficient, large-model text generation represents a performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 2.66 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48as_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio that makes it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without requiring the expense of dedicated GPU hardware. The combination of 384.0 GB of RAM, strong multi-core processing, and local storage capabilities makes this server well-suited for relational database management systems, in-memory caching layers, data analytics, and enterprise-grade web serving. It is also appropriate for moderate machine learning inference tasks, provided the model size does not exceed the memory bandwidth limits highlighted in large-model benchmarks.
